Buying guide

Condo or detached along Yonge: the cost trade-offs

The price gap is the smaller part of the comparison. Fees, upkeep, risk and exit decide which one is cheaper to own.

Ali Bayat
Figures checked against the sources below on November 21, 2026
4-minute readNorth York to Richmond HillUpdated November 2026
The short version
  • A condo swaps upkeep you control for fees you don't. A detached home does the reverse.
  • Land transfer tax is the same for both at the same price in the same municipality. It changes at Steeles Avenue, not with the building type.
  • The question that settles it is the monthly all-in cost plus what happens if you need to sell in five years.

01Two ways to own along the corridor

Condo

Sheppard-Yonge, North York Centre, Finch, VMC

Works best when

  • You want a short walk to the subway or Viva
  • You prefer a fixed monthly fee to unpredictable repairs
  • You plan to live there or rent it out with the building's rules in mind

Watch out for

  • Fees can rise, and the reserve fund decides how much
  • A special assessment can land on you after you buy
  • Rental or pet rules are set by the building

Detached or semi

Interior streets, Thornhill, Richmond Hill

Works best when

  • You want land, space or the option to renovate
  • You prefer to control repairs and timing
  • You value a lot that can carry value on its own

Watch out for

  • Repairs are yours: roof, furnace, foundation, water
  • Property tax and insurance are higher in dollar terms
  • Added units and rebuilds depend on zoning and permits

02What you pay, line by line

CostCondoDetached
Monthly feesCondo fees, set by the corporation's budgetNone
Property taxYes, on a smaller assessed valueYes, usually the larger bill
Repairs and upkeepInside the unit; the building handles the rest through feesAll of it, so set aside a yearly budget
Land transfer taxSame schedule; Toronto adds its own, York Region doesn'tSame schedule; Toronto adds its own, York Region doesn't
Biggest surpriseA special assessment or a fee jumpA large repair found after closing
How to checkRead the status certificate with your lawyerBook a full inspection and ask about permits
Selling laterYou compete with other units in your own buildingYou compete on the lot, the street and the condition
Ali's take

Don't compare the price. Compare what you'd pay each month for five years, plus the one big risk each type carries. The answer is often different from the one the price tag gives.

Quick answers

Which is cheaper to close on?

At the same price in the same municipality, the land transfer tax is the same. A condo adds a status certificate review. A detached home adds survey and title work, and an inspection is wise for both.

Which is better for an investor?

It depends on rent against fees for a condo, and on what zoning and permits allow for a house. Run both through the deal screen on the Invest page before comparing.

Torn between the two?

I'll run both on monthly cost, closing cost and resale for the exact homes you're considering.
